source: I’ve always been facinated by the tree line of BBQ: as one moves north, at what latitude does BBQ consumption plummet? The answer: roughly between the 36th parallel north and 37th.
why: The file has county FIPS GEOID and county name only, with no latitude/longitude or any other geographic coordinate, so the latitude at which BBQ share drops cannot be computed.

source: Pizza must have more competition as you move south and west (i.e., better BBQ and Mexican options).
why: The file records cuisine shares by county but no coordinates or region/state labels beyond the FIPS state prefix, so a south/west trend in pizza share cannot be computed from it.

why: The file is one row per county (FIPS GEOID and county NAME) with cuisine shares; it has no metropolitan-area identifier and no county-to-metro crosswalk or visit/population weights, so the story's city rankings cannot be rebuilt. Ranking counties instead gives different leaders (for example, the highest pizza county is Costilla County, CO at 100%, not Detroit).
